principle: The product does not prescribe what a repository should become; it identifies and strengthens the foundations that allow each repository to succeed at what it is intended to be.
refinementRule: Domains and kinds are data, not a taxonomy. Add, split, merge or re-weight one here; every change stays covered by the foundation-domains.json integrity gate and the module-smoke fixture set. Never add a domain the product cannot evidence from visible repository state, and never let a conclusion cite the absence of findings as evidence.

conclusions.strengthen: A domain is missing, weak or unclear, and a preview-first next action is offered.
conclusions.appropriate-as-is: Every applicable domain is present, or the repository is archived, intentionally minimal or externally managed - and the evidence says why.
conclusions.insufficiently-understood: The product cannot reach a conclusion and names what it would need. A finding about the product, not the repository.

domains.title: Documentation
domains.question: Can a newcomer understand and use this repository from what is written down?

domains.title: Purpose
domains.question: Is it clear what this repository is for and who it serves?
domains.note: The README contract's Overview/Usage section check is skipped under the doc-standards v1 schema, so purpose reads from readmeScore until the section check surfaces as its own signal.

nextAction.label: Preview a README that states the purpose

domains.title: Planning
domains.question: Is there a credible plan or roadmap for what comes next?

actionsByCase.note: 3.7 M4c: one action per kind of planning gap. The case is the branch the planning evaluator took (Portfolio.Conclusion.ps1 _PC_EvaluateDomain); every case it can emit must be mapped here or the conclusion contract fails. Routes must be flows the console can run (frontend/lib/foundationConclusion.ts RUNNABLE_NEXT_ACTION_ROUTES). The repair flow refuses missing, prose, empty and complete roadmaps, so only below-contract-ready is sent there.

no-roadmap.label: Draft a roadmap from the code and docs

prose-roadmap.label: Preview the plan rewritten as checklist milestones

parse-error.label: Preview a plan reconstructed from the repository
parse-error.observedNote: Fixture only. The parser reads parse-error as an empty ROADMAP.md; no cohort repository carries one.

complete-below-contract-ready.label: Preview candidate items for a next release

pendingWorkAction.label: Check the top-value item is ready to package
pendingWorkAction.note: Offered when every applicable domain is present and pending work is recorded: the packaging flow, preview-first - a readiness verdict, never a dispatch.

domains.title: Structure
domains.question: Is the layout maintainable and navigable by intent?

domains.title: Intentional engineering
domains.question: Is there evidence the work is deliberate - tests, CI, releases, conventions?

evidenceModel.decision: Defined, not scored. Release 3.7's ten repositories decide which evidence earns a detector; until then the domain reports what it observes without judging it.

subAreas.evidence: A test tree or test-runner configuration exists.
A CI workflow or pipeline definition exists.
The latest Actions run concluded successfully; pull requests are not piling up unreviewed.
Recent commits; a clean tree; work on the default branch or a named branch.
Conventions written down (CONTRIBUTING, lint and format configuration) and a layering the tree makes visible.
Tags or releases and a changelog that names them.

kinds.title: Not yet classified
kinds.note: No kind signal; every scored domain applies. A curation or classifier signal refines this.

kinds.title: Application
kinds.note: Release 3.7 M4a: a served page, an app-framework manifest, an executable project, or a README that says so. M4b decides what this kind is not judged on.

kinds.title: Firmware
kinds.note: Release 3.7 M4a: a firmware target (platformio.ini, Arduino sketch, ESP sdkconfig) or a README that says so.

kinds.title: Experiment

applicability.planning: An experiment plans by trying; a roadmap is optional until it has a direction. Experiments never meant to be finished are a normal state of this portfolio, not a gap (steering Rung 1).

applicabilityBasis.note: 3.7 M4b default, recorded as D-021. No cohort repository resolves experiment yet (2026-06-13_Orchestration's root carries no wording); fixture only. A cohort observation or Ben's ruling on D-021 changes this row, never code.

kinds.note: Release 3.7 M4a: the README purpose line calls it an experiment, prototype, spike or bootstrap. Provisional by nature; D-006 owner intent may overrule it.

kinds.title: Tooling
kinds.note: Release 3.7 M4a: a CLI entry, loose root scripts with no module manifest, or a README that calls it a tool or utility.

applicability.planning: A minimal utility with no pending work needs no roadmap.

applicabilityBasis.note: Release 3.6 M1 starting set; module-smoke fixture 'minimal-utility'. No detection rule resolves minimal yet, so no cohort repository has carried it.

kinds.title: Externally managed

applicability.planning: Plans live with the upstream owner.

applicabilityBasis.note: Release 3.6 M1 starting set. External management is owner intent (D-006); the trial recorded the category as unrepresented, so no repository has carried it.

kinds.reason: Externally managed: the upstream owner decides its plan and layout.

kinds.title: Archived

applicability.planning: An archived repository plans no further work.
applicability.structure: An archived repository is not reorganized.
applicability.intentional-engineering: An archived repository is not judged on ongoing engineering.

applicabilityBasis.note: Release 3.6 M1 starting set; observed on the trial's curated archive (curationState archived-ignore), which concludes appropriate-as-is with planning, structure and intentional-engineering not applicable.

kinds.reason: Archived: intentionally closed, kept for reference.

lifecycleConsistency.note: Steering extension 3 (Rung 1): lifecycleState (Portfolio.Assessment.ps1 _ResolveLifecycleState) and conclusion (this model) are two verdicts over the same signals and may not disagree without saying why. `allowed` lists, per lifecycle state, the conclusions that agree with it. Any other pair must match an `exceptions` entry whose `requires` pattern is found in the record's basis lines or its domain=status facts; the match is the explanation's evidence. A pair with no allowed entry and no matching exception is a contract violation (Test-FoundationConclusion). A lifecycle state not listed here is a violation too.

exceptions.explanation: The lifecycle names a state, but the product could not read enough to conclude - no local checkout, a failed scan, or a plan it cannot parse - and the conclusion says what it needs before it can agree.
The lifecycle reads a missing README as blocking; the kind's applicability says documentation is not this repository's to have, or a kind rule concludes for it.
The lifecycle reads a missing roadmap as blocking; the kind's applicability says planning is not this repository's to have, or a kind rule concludes for it.

The lifecycle reads an insufficient execution contract as blocking; the kind's applicability says planning is not this repository's to have, or a kind rule (archived by curation, externally managed) concludes for it. The lifecycle model does not read curation; this model does.
The lifecycle reads open structure findings as blocking; the kind's applicability says structure is not this repository's to have, or a kind rule concludes for it.

hintKinds.note: Which kind each hint speaks for. Read by the coherence observation (steering extension 2): when the manifest hints and the README wording hints name kinds that share nothing, the disagreement is emitted as an observation with canonicalEffect none. It changes no verdict.

kindDetection.note: Only signals the index already carries. Every matching rule is a ranked candidate and the first is the kind; each rule names the repositories it was observed on (steering section 5); `when` is field equality, `whenAny` is 'this dotted path holds one of these values' (kindSignals.hints comes from Portfolio.KindSignals.ps1 at scan time). Anything undetected is 'unknown' - honest, and every scored domain applies.

rules.basis: a firmware target is checked in (platformio.ini, Arduino sketch or ESP sdkconfig)
the README purpose line calls it an experiment, prototype, spike or bootstrap
a served page or app framework outranks a helper module in the same repository: a served page, an app-framework dependency or an executable project
the manifest declares a module or publishable package
the README purpose line names a firmware target
the manifest declares a command-line entry
the README purpose line calls it a library, module, client or wrapper
the README purpose line calls it an application, site, dashboard or engine
the README purpose line calls it a tool or utility, or loose scripts sit at the root with no module manifest
